faq.q: What should I check on a large Surrey property near farmland or the coast?
faq.a: Two parcel-level checks: ALR status, through the Agricultural Land Commission's maps and online mapping tools; and floodplain status, since the City puts about 20% of Surrey's land area in its coastal floodplain, names Crescent Beach and Panorama/Gray Creek among its residential areas, and notes most of the floodplain is dyke-protected.

faq.q: Can I add a suite or coach house to a house in Surrey?
faq.a: BC's small-scale multi-unit housing rules allow more homes on many urban lots, but each municipality sets the details and many lots are excluded. Check the lot's zoning with the municipality before you plan a suite or coach house.

faq.q: Do I need a home inspection when buying in Surrey?
faq.a: It is strongly recommended. Make the offer subject to an inspection so a qualified inspector can look at the roof, structure, drainage, electrical and heating before you remove conditions.

faq.q: How do I find out which school serves an address in Surrey?
faq.a: School catchments are set by address, so use the school district's catchment locator with the exact address. Catchment lines change, so check before you write an offer.
